headline: Medium pairwise risk: RD-Agent’s browser/API egress can amplify Prefect-driven workflow outputs into leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not established. However, Prefect can orchestrate workflow metadata and RD-Agent can run browsers and consume external content, so a manual copy/paste or file bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF Prefect outputs are manually copied into RD-Agent prompts or browser inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy/paste of untrusted workflow text into RD-Agent prompts.
Add a short human review step before any RD-Agent action on Prefect output.
Use a provenance tag on all Prefect-generated text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect has broad network egress and RD-Agent handles sensitive classes including financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets. Even without a shared workspace, RD-Agent’s API calls and browser use create a plausible path for sensitive material to leave the pair through external services. The interaction is inferred from docs-only evidence, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Prefect passes workflow metadata containing sensitive identifiers into RD-Agent tasks, leakage risk increases.
IF RD-Agent processes competition datasets or logs through external APIs, those contents may be exposed.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a non-sensitive test dataset.
Turn off any optional uploads or browser-based data submission in RD-Agent.
Review Prefect task inputs for secrets before handoff.
Separate credentials so neither agent can reuse the other’s API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction at the orchestration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect can orchestrate workflows and RD-Agent supports multiple instances with broad egress and browser/API use. That creates overlapping control over mutable external resources and concurrent execution, which can conflict if both touch the same repo, dataset, or API quota. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository, dataset, or API-backed resource, conflicts can occur.
IF Prefect schedules parallel RD-Agent instances against the same target, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only access where possible.
Set per-agent API quotas.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can generate workflow metadata that RD-Agent may treat as input for research or development actions, and RD-Agent can then act through APIs or browsers. Because no verification step between them is documented, an error in Prefect output could propagate into RD-Agent’s downstream actions. The blast radius is broader than a single document, but not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Prefect-produced metadata as authoritative, errors can cascade.
IF RD-Agent uses that input to trigger browser or API actions, downstream mistakes multiply.
mitigations: Require a human approval step before RD-Agent acts on Prefect output.
Add schema validation to Prefect outputs.
Log and diff RD-Agent inputs against source data.
Use a small canary workflow first.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and secrets and sends data to third-party APIs. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention, residency, and third-party processing, even though no specific jurisdiction is documented. Because the evidence is docs-only and the exact policy gap is unspecified, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is routed through RD-Agent APIs, residency or DPA issues may arise.
IF Prefect workflow metadata includes retention-sensitive identifiers, mismatched logging policies can violate internal policy.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to either agent.
Block regulated data from RD-Agent until a DPA is confirmed.
Shorten log retention for both agents.
Review vendor terms for each external API.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
